detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Add a config-driven hook, `data.custom_validation_metrics.{path,name}`, that lets users add validation metrics without subclassing the trainer.

Built-in validation metrics are grouped only by `data_source` and use fixed statistics (mean/std/best/worst/maj @N). Metrics split by another per-sample attribute, or metrics that combine several fields, currently require overriding `_val_metrics_update` in a trainer subclass. The new hook is loaded with `load_extern_object`, like `custom_reward_function` and `data.custom_cls`. It covers both the legacy `RayPPOTrainer` and the V1 `PPOTrainer`, and it is disabled by default, so behavior is unchanged unless it is configured.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [custom validation metrics](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+custom+validation+metrics), [_val_metrics_update](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+_val_metrics_update), [process_validation_metrics](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+process_validation_metrics). No open PR adds such a hook. Related PRs with a different scope: #7240 adds a built-in pass@k metric (it touches the same files, so a textual conflict is possible), #8113 adds validation sampling profiles, and #6845 fixes a sparse-key crash.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13):

```bash
RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV=0 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest \
  tests/trainer/ppo/test_custom_validation_metrics_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_metric_utils_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_import_utils_on_cpu.py tests/experimental/fully_async_policy/test_async_genrm_config_on_cpu.py -q
# 64 passed

# each tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_*_on_cpu.py file, run separately
# 229 passed in total
```

For both trainers, the new `test_custom_validation_metrics_on_cpu.py` calls the real `_val_metrics_update` and checks that:

- built-in metrics are unchanged and the custom metrics are merged;
- the function receives `data_sources` as a `list` and the exact per-sample `reward_extra_infos` dict;
- a disabled hook produces only the built-in metrics;
- a non-dict return value raises `TypeError`, and a key collision with a built-in metric raises `ValueError`;
- invalid configs (missing `name`, missing file, missing attribute, non-callable object) fail at load time;
- constructing `RayPPOTrainer` or the V1 `PPOTrainer` from a composed `ppo_trainer` config with a wrong function name fails during construction.

No GPU or end-to-end run was done. The change only affects validation-metric post-processing and is a no-op when disabled.

### API and Usage Example

```python
# my_metrics.py
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np


def difficulty_metrics(data_sources: list[str], reward_extra_infos: dict[str, list]) -> dict[str, float]:
    acc_by_difficulty = defaultdict(list)
    for difficulty, acc in zip(reward_extra_infos["difficulty"], reward_extra_infos["acc"], strict=True):
        acc_by_difficulty[difficulty].append(acc)
    return {f"val-aux/difficulty/{key}/acc/mean": float(np.mean(vals)) for key, vals in acc_by_difficulty.items()}
```

```bash
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo ... \
  data.custom_validation_metrics.path=/path/to/my_metrics.py \
  data.custom_validation_metrics.name=difficulty_metrics
```

- `data_sources`: the data source of each validation sample.
- `reward_extra_infos`: the same per-sample dict passed to `process_validation_metrics` (`reward`, `acc` and any extra reward fields).
- The returned dict is merged into the validation metrics, and its keys are used verbatim.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/ppo/metric_utils.py`:
  - `load_custom_validation_metrics_fn(data_config)` returns `None` when `path` is unset, raises `ValueError` if `name` is missing, and raises `TypeError` if the object is not callable.
  - `merge_custom_validation_metrics(...)` calls the function, raises `TypeError` on a non-dict result and `ValueError` on a collision with a built-in key.
- `RayPPOTrainer` and the V1 `PPOTrainer` load the function in `__init__`, so a wrong path or name fails at startup instead of after the first validation rollout. The result is merged at the end of `_val_metrics_update`, which also covers the legacy `_merge_validation_results` path.
- `OneStepOffRayTrainer` and `FullyAsyncRollouter` override `__init__` without calling `RayPPOTrainer.__init__` but still use the inherited `_validate`. Each gets one line that loads the function the same way, so validation keeps working and the option is honored.
- `verl/trainer/config/data/legacy_data.yaml` and the regenerated `_generated_*.yaml`: new `custom_validation_metrics: {path: null, name: null}` next to `custom_cls`.
- `docs/examples/config.rst`: new "Customized Validation Metrics" section.

#### Open questions for reviewers

- Should the function also receive `sample_uids` and `sample_turns` (e.g. for per-prompt metrics such as pass@k)? The current `fn(data_sources=..., reward_extra_infos=...)` signature matches an existing user function; more inputs could be added later as optional keyword arguments.
- Should custom keys be namespaced automatically (e.g. a `val-custom/` prefix) instead of being used verbatim with only a collision check?
- Is `data.*` the right place, or would `trainer.*` be preferred?

AI assistance (Cursor) was used to write the code, tests and this description. This is a draft: the submitter is reviewing every changed line and will mark it ready after that review.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks: `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passed all hooks.
- [x] Add / Update the documentation: `docs/examples/config.rst`.
- [x] Add unit tests: `tests/trainer/ppo/test_custom_validation_metrics_on_cpu.py` is collected by `cpu_unit_tests.yml`.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.
- [x] Not related to the `recipe` submodule.

 - ``data.custom_cls.path``: The path to the file containing your customized dataset class. If not specified, pre-implemented dataset will be used.
 - ``data.custom_cls.name``: The name of the dataset class within the specified file.
 
+Customized Validation Metrics
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+Built-in validation metrics are grouped by ``data_source`` only. To add other aggregations without
+subclassing the trainer, point ``data.custom_validation_metrics`` to a function. It is supported by both
+the legacy ``RayPPOTrainer`` and the V1 ``PPOTrainer``.
+
+.. code:: yaml
+
+   custom_validation_metrics:
+     path: null
+     name: null
+
+- ``data.custom_validation_metrics.path``: The path to the file containing the function. If not specified,
+  only built-in validation metrics are computed.
+- ``data.custom_validation_metrics.name``: The name of the function within the specified file. Required when
+  ``path`` is set.
+
+The function is loaded when the trainer is constructed and called once per validation as
+``fn(data_sources=..., reward_extra_infos=...)``:
+
+- ``data_sources``: ``list[str]``, the data source of each validation sample.
+- ``reward_extra_infos``: ``dict[str, list]``, the per-sample values also used by the built-in metrics,
+  i.e. ``reward`` plus every extra field returned by the reward function (e.g. ``acc``).
+
+It must return a ``dict`` mapping metric names to scalar values. The keys are logged verbatim, so choose a
+prefix such as ``val-aux/`` to group them with the built-in metrics. For example, to report the mean ``acc``
+per ``difficulty`` returned by the reward function:
+
+.. code:: python
+
+   from collections import defaultdict
+
+   import numpy as np
+
+
+   def difficulty_metrics(data_sources: list[str], reward_extra_infos: dict[str, list]) -> dict[str, float]:
+       acc_by_difficulty = defaultdict(list)
+       for difficulty, acc in zip(reward_extra_infos["difficulty"], reward_extra_infos["acc"], strict=True):
+           acc_by_difficulty[difficulty].append(acc)
+       return {f"val-aux/difficulty/{key}/acc/mean": float(np.mean(vals)) for key, vals in acc_by_difficulty.items()}
+
+.. code:: bash
+
+   data.custom_validation_metrics.path=/path/to/my_metrics.py \
+   data.custom_validation_metrics.name=difficulty_metrics
+
+A wrong ``path`` or ``name`` fails at trainer construction. During validation, a non-``dict`` return value
+raises ``TypeError`` and a key that collides with a built-in validation metric raises ``ValueError``.
+
 Actor/Rollout/Reference Policy
 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

+from collections.abc import Callable

+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+from hydra import compose, initialize_config_module
+from omegaconf import DictConfig, OmegaConf
+
+from verl.trainer.ppo.metric_utils import CustomValidationMetricsFn, load_custom_validation_metrics_fn
+from verl.trainer.ppo.ray_trainer import RayPPOTrainer
+from verl.trainer.ppo.utils import Role
+from verl.trainer.ppo.v1.trainer_base import PPOTrainer
+
+_METRICS_MODULE = """
+LAST_CALL = {}
+
+
+def difficulty_metrics(data_sources, reward_extra_infos):
+    LAST_CALL["data_sources"] = data_sources
+    LAST_CALL["reward_extra_infos"] = reward_extra_infos
+    accs = {}
+    for difficulty, acc in zip(reward_extra_infos["difficulty"], reward_extra_infos["acc"], strict=True):
+        accs.setdefault(difficulty, []).append(acc)
+    return {f"val-aux/difficulty/{key}/acc/mean": sum(vals) / len(vals) for key, vals in accs.items()}
+
+
+def not_a_dict(data_sources, reward_extra_infos):
+    return [1.0]
+
+
+def builtin_collision(data_sources, reward_extra_infos):
+    return {"val-aux/num_turns/mean": 0.0}
+
+
+NOT_CALLABLE = 1
+"""
+
+DATA_SOURCES = ["math", "math", "code", "code"]
+SAMPLE_UIDS = ["u0", "u0", "u1", "u1"]
+SAMPLE_TURNS = [1, 2, 3, 4]
+
+ValMetricsUpdate = Callable[[CustomValidationMetricsFn | None, dict[str, list[Any]]], dict[str, Any]]
+
+
+class _StubV1Trainer(PPOTrainer):
+    def on_step_end(self):
+        pass
+
+    def on_sample_end(self):
+        pass
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def metrics_module(tmp_path: Path) -> str:
+    module_path = tmp_path / "my_metrics.py"
+    module_path.write_text(_METRICS_MODULE)
+    return str(module_path)
+
+
+def _load(path: str | None, name: str | None) -> CustomValidationMetricsFn | None:
+    return load_custom_validation_metrics_fn(
+        OmegaConf.create({"custom_validation_metrics": {"path": path, "name": name}})
+    )
+
+
+def _reward_extra_infos() -> dict[str, list[Any]]:
+    return {
+        "reward": [1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0],
+        "acc": [1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0],
+        "difficulty": ["easy", "hard", "hard", "hard"],
+    }
+
+
+def _legacy_val_metrics(
+    custom_fn: CustomValidationMetricsFn | None, reward_extra_infos: dict[str, list[Any]]
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    trainer = RayPPOTrainer.__new__(RayPPOTrainer)
+    trainer.custom_validation_metrics_fn = custom_fn
+    return trainer._val_metrics_update(
+        np.array(DATA_SOURCES, dtype=object),
+        SAMPLE_UIDS,
+        reward_extra_infos,
+        [np.array(SAMPLE_TURNS[:2]), np.array(SAMPLE_TURNS[2:])],
+    )
+
+
+def _v1_val_metrics(
+    custom_fn: CustomValidationMetricsFn | None, reward_extra_infos: dict[str, list[Any]]
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    trainer = _StubV1Trainer.__new__(_StubV1Trainer)
+    trainer.custom_validation_metrics_fn = custom_fn
+    return trainer._val_metrics_update(list(DATA_SOURCES), SAMPLE_UIDS, reward_extra_infos, SAMPLE_TURNS)
+
+
+both_trainers = pytest.mark.parametrize("val_metrics", [_legacy_val_metrics, _v1_val_metrics], ids=["legacy", "v1"])
+
+
+@both_trainers
+def test_custom_metrics_are_merged_with_builtin_metrics(metrics_module: str, val_metrics: ValMetricsUpdate) -> None:
+    custom_fn = _load(metrics_module, "difficulty_metrics")
+    reward_extra_infos = _reward_extra_infos()
+
+    builtin = val_metrics(None, _reward_extra_infos())
+    merged = val_metrics(custom_fn, reward_extra_infos)
+
+    assert "val-core/math/acc/mean@2" in builtin
+    assert "val-aux/num_turns/mean" in builtin
+    assert {key: merged[key] for key in builtin} == builtin
+    assert {key: merged[key] for key in merged.keys() - builtin.keys()} == {
+        "val-aux/difficulty/easy/acc/mean": 1.0,
+        "val-aux/difficulty/hard/acc/mean": pytest.approx(2 / 3),
+    }
+
+    last_call = custom_fn.__globals__["LAST_CALL"]
+    assert type(last_call["data_sources"]) is list
+    assert last_call["data_sources"] == DATA_SOURCES
+    assert last_call["reward_extra_infos"] is reward_extra_infos
+
+
+@both_trainers
+def test_disabled_hook_only_produces_builtin_metrics(val_metrics: ValMetricsUpdate) -> None:
+    assert _load(None, None) is None
+    assert load_custom_validation_metrics_fn(OmegaConf.create({})) is None
+
+    metrics = val_metrics(None, _reward_extra_infos())
+
+    assert all(key.startswith(("val-core/", "val-aux/")) for key in metrics)
+    assert not any("difficulty" in key for key in metrics)
+
+
+@both_trainers
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("fn_name", "error", "match"),
+    [("not_a_dict", TypeError, "must return a dict"), ("builtin_collision", ValueError, "val-aux/num_turns/mean")],
+)
+def test_invalid_custom_metrics_fail(
+    metrics_module: str, val_metrics: ValMetricsUpdate, fn_name: str, error: type[Exception], match: str
+) -> None:
+    with pytest.raises(error, match=match):
+        val_metrics(_load(metrics_module, fn_name), _reward_extra_infos())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("path", "name", "error"),
+    [
+        ("{module}", None, ValueError),
+        ("{module}", "missing_fn", AttributeError),
+        ("{module}", "NOT_CALLABLE", TypeError),
+        ("/nonexistent/my_metrics.py", "difficulty_metrics", FileNotFoundError),
+    ],
+)
+def test_bad_config_fails_at_load(metrics_module: str, path: str, name: str | None, error: type[Exception]) -> None:
+    with pytest.raises(error):
+        _load(path.format(module=metrics_module), name)
+
+
+def _trainer_config(metrics_module: str, fn_name: str) -> DictConfig:
+    overrides = [
+        f"data.custom_validation_metrics.path={metrics_module}",
+        f"data.custom_validation_metrics.name={fn_name}",
+    ]
+    with initialize_config_module(config_module="verl.trainer.config", version_base=None):
+        return compose(config_name="ppo_trainer", overrides=overrides)
+
+
+def test_legacy_trainer_construction_fails_on_bad_name(metrics_module: str) -> None:
+    config = _trainer_config(metrics_module, "missing_fn")
+    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="missing_fn"):
+        RayPPOTrainer(
+            config=config,
+            tokenizer=None,
+            role_worker_mapping={Role.ActorRollout: object},
+            resource_pool_manager=None,
+        )
+
+
+def test_v1_trainer_construction_fails_on_bad_name(metrics_module: str) -> None:
+    config = _trainer_config(metrics_module, "missing_fn")
+    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="missing_fn"):
+        _StubV1Trainer(config)

+CustomValidationMetricsFn = Callable[..., dict[str, Any]]

+def load_custom_validation_metrics_fn(data_config: DictConfig) -> CustomValidationMetricsFn | None:
+    """Load the user function configured by ``data.custom_validation_metrics``.
+
+    Args:
+        data_config: The ``data`` section of the trainer config.
+
+    Returns:
+        The loaded function, or ``None`` if ``data.custom_validation_metrics.path`` is not set.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If ``path`` is set but ``name`` is not.
+        TypeError: If the loaded object is not callable.
+    """
+    fn_config = data_config.get("custom_validation_metrics") or {}
+    module_path = fn_config.get("path")
+    if not module_path:
+        return None
+
+    fn_name = fn_config.get("name")
+    if not fn_name:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"data.custom_validation_metrics.name must be set when data.custom_validation_metrics.path={module_path!r}"
+        )
+
+    fn = load_extern_object(module_path=module_path, object_name=fn_name)
+    if not callable(fn):
+        raise TypeError(f"Custom validation metrics {fn_name!r} from {module_path!r} must be callable, got {type(fn)}")
+    return fn
+
+
+def merge_custom_validation_metrics(
+    metric_dict: dict[str, Any],
+    custom_metrics_fn: CustomValidationMetricsFn,
+    data_sources: list[str],
+    reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list[Any]],
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Call a custom validation metrics function and merge its result into the built-in metrics.
+
+    The function is called as ``custom_metrics_fn(data_sources=..., reward_extra_infos=...)`` with the
+    same per-sample inputs as :func:`process_validation_metrics`. Returned keys are used verbatim as
+    metric names.
+
+    Args:
+        metric_dict: Built-in validation metrics.
+        custom_metrics_fn: Function returned by :func:`load_custom_validation_metrics_fn`.
+        data_sources: Data source of each validation sample.
+        reward_extra_infos_dict: Per-sample reward values and extra reward infos.
+
+    Returns:
+        A new dict with the built-in and custom metrics.
+
+    Raises:
+        TypeError: If the custom function does not return a dict.
+        ValueError: If a custom metric key collides with a built-in metric key.
+    """
+    custom_metrics = custom_metrics_fn(data_sources=list(data_sources), reward_extra_infos=reward_extra_infos_dict)
+    if not isinstance(custom_metrics, dict):
+        raise TypeError(f"Custom validation metrics must return a dict, got {type(custom_metrics)}")
+
+    collisions = sorted(metric_dict.keys() & custom_metrics.keys())
+    if collisions:
+        raise ValueError(f"Custom validation metrics collide with built-in validation metrics: {collisions}")
+    return metric_dict | custom_metrics

# Contributor License Agreement (CLA) assistant

Streamline your workflow and let CLA assistant handle the legal side of contributions to a repository for you. CLA assistant enables contributors to sign CLAs from within a pull request.

To get started, simply store your CLA as a GitHub Gist file then link it with the repository/organisation in CLA assistant. Then sit back and relax while CLA assistant:

- Comments on each opened pull request to ask the contributor to sign the CLA
- Allows contributors to sign a CLA from within a pull request
- Authenticates the signee with their GitHub account
- Updates the status of a pull request when the contributor agrees to the CLA
- Automatically asks users to re-sign the CLA for each new pull request in the event the associated Gist & CLA has changed
- Green lights merge queues without additional CLA checks as everyone needs to have signed of on the PR level already

Repository owners can review a list of users who signed the CLA for each version of it. To get started, visit [cla-assistant.io](https://cla-assistant.io).
